item.title: Scored 31 of 100. The gap: form labels.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But 1987 form controls have no label.
The lesson for every team: Give every input a visible label tied to it with for and id. Screen readers announce it, and the tap target grows.
One automated analysis of public pages on 26 Oct 2026, requested through QA-lab URL Review. A starting point, not a verdict. item.title: Policía Nacional's search has no label.
item.description:
HSTS with preload, framing limited to its own origin, a declared language, and every internal link opened answered. But the home page search box and volume slider have no label, so screen readers announce blank fields.
The lesson for every team: Tie each field to a <label for>, or give it an aria-label. A screen reader can only announce a name that exists.

item.title: Measure the action, not just the visit.
item.description:
Page views tell you someone arrived. An event on the form, the download, or the signup tells you whether the page worked.
Try this today: Pick the one action each key page exists for. Make sure an event fires only when it succeeds.

item.description:
